Targeted literature review with interpretation and perspective METHODS: We performed a review of selected literature describing immune-mediated retinal and choroidal adverse reactions associated with ICI therapy, synthesizing and categorizing the likely underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Based on these mechanistic categories, we provide perspective on a rational approach to the evaluation of patients with ICI-associated inflammatory disorders of the retina and choroid.

Results

ICI-induced posterior segment adverse reactions can be categorized into 3 major mechanisms of unintended, targeted inflammation that share similarities to immunotherapy-related adverse events (irAEs) seen in other organ systems. In Type 1 reactions, T cell activation by ICIs can result in cross-reactivity of anti-tumor T cells with ocular tissues (Type 1a) or expansion of eye-specific T cells in predisposed individuals (Type 1b), leading to ocular inflammation that mimics known uveitic conditions. In Type 2 reactions, nonspecific ocular or systemic inflammation exacerbated by ICI use can cause retinal vasculitis through a "bystander" mechanism, potentially resulting in vision-threatening vascular occlusions. Finally, in Type 3 reactions, ICI use can prompt autoantibody-mediated inflammation and/or exacerbation of paraneoplastic processes likely related to T cell driven expansion of B cell populations.

Conclusions

Although relatively uncommon, posterior segment inflammatory disorders associated with systemic ICI therapy may be vision-threatening if not identified and treated appropriately. We propose that the pathogenic mechanisms underlying these chorioretinopathies falls into 3 major categories involving inadvertent T cell mediated inflammation. Visual prognosis with appropriate treatment is generally favorable, but some reactions, such as longstanding exudative retinal detachments and ICI-induced occlusive retinal vasculitis, can result in permanent visual defects.

records.title: A comprehensive scoping review of methodological approaches and clinical applications of tear fluid biomarkers.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: A comprehensive scoping review of methodological approaches and clinical applications of tear fluid biomarkers.
content.abstract: Tear fluid is an emerging source of disease biomarkers, drawing attention due to its quick, inexpensive, and non-invasive collection. The advancements in detection techniques enable the measurement of ultra-low biomarker levels from small sample volumes typical of tear fluid. The lack of standardized protocols for collection, processing, and analysis of tear fluid remains a significant challenge. To address this, we convened the Tear Research Network Review Taskforce in 2022 to review protocols from the past three decades, providing a comprehensive overview of the methodologies used in tear fluid biomarker research. A total of 1484 articles published from January 1974 to May 2024 from two electronic databases, Embase and Ovid MEDLINE, were reviewed. An exponential increase in the number of articles on tear fluid biomarkers was observed from 2015 onwards. The two most commonly reported collection methods were; glass capillaries (45.2%), and Schirmer's strips (25%), with glass capillary tube collection remaining the most frequent method until 2019, when Schirmer's strips became the leading method. Most articles analyzed tear fluid proteins (65%) and focused on a single analyte (32.3%). In recent years, an increase was observed in the type and number of examined analytes. The differences in the reported methodologies and protocols underscore the need for standardization and harmonization within the field of tear fluid biomarkers to minimize methodological differences and reduce variability in clinical outcomes. Consistent and detailed reporting is essential for improving the reproducibility and validity of tear fluid studies, in order to advance their potential clinical applications.

records.title: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF DISEASE PROGRESSION REPORTED IN RPGR -ASSOCIATED X-LINKED RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA.

content.title: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF DISEASE PROGRESSION REPORTED IN RPGR -ASSOCIATED X-LINKED RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Retinitis pigmentosa GTPase regulator-associated X-linked retinitis pigmentosa ( RPGR -associated XLRP) is a rare and severe form of retinitis pigmentosa, resulting in progressive visual impairment; however, disease progression data are limited. A systematic literature review was conducted to assess available data on disease progression in RPGR -associated XLRP.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and select congress abstracts were evaluated through June 2022. Eligible studies included results specific to RPGR -associated XLRP or populations with ≥80% of patients with retinitis pigmentosa carrying disease-causing RPGR variants. End points of interest included visual acuity, visual field, ellipsoid zone width, progression to blindness, and patient-reported outcomes.

Results

Fourteen studies met ≥1 end point of interest. Progressive declines in visual acuity, visual field, and ellipsoid zone width were reported across studies. Nearly all publications reported annual declines in visual acuity (3.5%-8.2%). Annual visual field declines ranged from 4.2% to 13.3%. Changes in retinal structure were also observed (ellipsoid zone width changes: -177 to -830 µ m/year). Most studies measured blindness using visual acuity; visual field-based definitions resulted in blindness by age ∼25 years. Patient-reported outcome data were limited.

Conclusion

Published evidence shows that patients with RPGR -associated XLRP experience progressive decline in visual acuity, visual field, and ellipsoid zone width, eventually resulting in blindness. Additional longitudinal data with standardized end points and expanded collection of patient-reported outcomes are needed to assess visual decline in RPGR -associated XLRP.

records.title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Age-Related Macular Degeneration Reveals 2 New Loci Implying Shared Genetic Components with Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

content.title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Age-Related Macular Degeneration Reveals 2 New Loci Implying Shared Genetic Components with Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the genetic architecture of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in a Japanese population.

Design

Genome-wide association study (GWAS).

Participants

Three thousand seven hundred seventy-two patients with AMD and 16 770 control participants from the Japanese population were enrolled in the association analyses.

Methods

We conducted a meta-analysis of 2 independent GWASs that included a total of 2663 patients with AMD and 9471 control participants using the imputation reference panel for genotype imputation specified for the Japanese population (n = 3541). A replication study was performed using an independent set of 1109 patients with AMD and 7299 control participants.

Main outcome measures

Associations of genetic variants with AMD.

Results

A meta-analysis of the 2 GWASs identified 6 loci significantly associated with AMD (P < 5.0 × 10-8). Of these loci, 4 were known to be associated with AMD (CFH, C2/FB, TNFRSF10A, and ARMS2), and 2 were novel (rs4147157 near WBP1L and rs76228488 near GATA5). The newly identified associations were confirmed in a replication study (P < 0.01). After the meta-analysis of all datasets, we observed strong associations in these loci (P = 1.88 × 10-12 and P = 1.35 × 10-9 for meta-analysis for rs4147157 and rs76228488, respectively). When we looked up the associations in the reported central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) GWAS conducted in the Japanese population, both loci were associated significantly with CSC (P = 4.86 × 10-3 and P = 4.28 × 10-3 for rs4147157 and rs76228488, respectively). We performed a genetic colocalization analysis for these loci and estimated that the posterior probabilities of shared causal variants between AMD and CSC were 0.39 and 0.60 for WBP1L and GATA5, respectively. Genetic correlation analysis focusing on the epidemiologically suggested clinical risk factors implicated shared polygenic architecture between AMD and smoking cessation (rg [the measure of genetic correlation] = -0.33; P = 0.01; false discovery rate, 0.099).

Conclusions

Our findings imply shared genetic components conferring the risk of both AMD and CSC.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: The role of CFTR in the eye, and the effect of early highly effective modulator treatment for cystic fibrosis on eye health.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The role of CFTR in the eye, and the effect of early highly effective modulator treatment for cystic fibrosis on eye health.
content.abstract: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) is a protein that plays a crucial role in various human organs, including the respiratory and digestive systems. Dysfunctional CFTR is the key variant of the lethal genetic disorder, cystic fibrosis (CF). In the past decade, highly effective CFTR modulator therapies, including elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor, have revolutionised CF management by correcting the underlying molecular defect to improve patient outcomes and life expectancy. Despite demonstrating multiorgan efficacy, clinical studies have largely overlooked the potential for ocular disturbances with CFTR modulator therapy, with the exception of a few case studies reporting the presence of crystalline lens pathologies in young children on CFTR modulators, and in breastfed infants born to individuals who were on CFTR modulator treatment during pregnancy. CFTR is present in multiple tissues during embryonic development, including the eye, and its expression can be influenced by genetic and environmental factors. This review summarises the role of CFTR in the eye, and the potential impact of CFTR on eye function and vision later in life. This information provides a framework for understanding the use and possible effects of CFTR-modulating therapeutics in the context of eye health, including the potential to leverage the eye for non-invasive and accessible diagnostic and monitoring capabilities in patients with CF.

records.title: ROLE OF OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE POSTERIOR VITREOUS DETACHMENT AND ITS COMPLICATIONS.

content.title: ROLE OF OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE POSTERIOR VITREOUS DETACHMENT AND ITS COMPLICATIONS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Currently, no consensus exists on the role of optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging in the setting of acute posterior vitreous detachment (PVD). The authors outline the clinical utility of OCT in the management of acute PVD and its complications.

Methods

Literature review of OCT findings in association with acute PVD and report of illustrative cases.

Results

Optical coherence tomography imaging in the setting of acute PVD can provide details of vitreoretinal interface that are difficult to appreciate on biomicroscopy alone including partial PVDs, focal vitreoretinal adhesions and traction, and subclinical macular changes. The presence of vitreous hyperreflective dots on OCT in the premacular space, especially if severe, is highly correlated with the presence of peripheral retinal breaks and development of epiretinal membrane. Advancements in OCT technology, including enhanced vitreous imaging OCT, swept-source OCT, wide-angle OCT, and widefield OCT, allow for increased resolution and expanded field of imaging of the vitreoretinal interface.

Conclusion

Optical coherence tomography imaging is an emerging standard of care in the setting of patients presenting with new flashes and floaters. The authors highlight the benefits of OCT imaging in patients with acute PVD, which includes recognition of the status of the vitreoretinal interface, assistance in identifying high-risk PVDs, and performance of risk assessment that predict future macular pathologic condition.

records.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
content.abstract: Over the last 20 years, research into the Meibomian glands of the eyelids has increased exponentially and is now widely recognized as a field of research. It is all the more astonishing that knowledge about another type of gland in the eyelids, the Moll glands or ciliary glands, has almost stagnated and there has been little to almost no progress, even though this type of gland as a whole takes up a relatively large volume in the upper and lower eyelids. There is not much information about the namesake Moll or the function of the glands although these are listed in nearly every textbook of anatomy, histology and ophthalmology. For this reason, we set out to compile the existing knowledge about the Moll glands of the eyelids in order to create a basis for follow-up studies and to stimulate research into this type of gland. In our literature research, we went back to the middle of the 19th century and made contact with a descendant of the Moll family and illustrate their relevance for the present. The structure of the secretory part of the Moll glands is very well described, a number of secretory products are known, but the current state of research allows only very rough speculations about their function. The overview provides numerous interesting insights, which, however, raise more questions than they provide answers.

records.title: Treatment of Noninfectious Uveitic Macular Edema with Periocular and Intraocular Corticosteroid Therapies: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Treatment of Noninfectious Uveitic Macular Edema with Periocular and Intraocular Corticosteroid Therapies: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the evidence on the effectiveness and complications of periocular and intraocular corticosteroid therapies for noninfectious uveitic macular edema.

Methods

A literature search of the PubMed database was conducted last in December 2021 and a post-assessment search was conducted in March 2023. The searches were limited to articles published in English and no date restrictions were imposed. The combined searches yielded 739 citations; 53 articles were selected for inclusion because the studies (1) evaluated periocular corticosteroid injection, intraocular corticosteroid injection or implant, suprachoroidal corticosteroid injection, or a combination thereof for uveitic macular edema; (2) had outcomes that included visual acuity (VA) or macular edema assessed clinically or imaged by OCT or fluorescein angiography; and (3) included more than 20 patients.

Results

This assessment reviewed 23 articles that provided level I or level II evidence from 18 studies on the use of periocular, suprachoroidal, and intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide injections and intravitreal dexamethasone and fluocinolone acetonide implants or inserts in noninfectious uveitic macular edema. These reports consistently demonstrated that all investigated periocular and intraocular corticosteroid therapies improved VA, macular structure, or both. One comparative study showed that intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide injection and the dexamethasone intravitreal implant had effectiveness superior to that of periocular triamcinolone acetonide injection for these outcomes. As a group, the studies highlighted the potential for these therapies to elevate intraocular pressure and to accelerate cataract formation.

Conclusions

The published literature provides high-quality evidence that periocular and intraocular corticosteroid therapies are effective and safe for the treatment of noninfectious uveitic macular edema. However, information on the relative effectiveness and complication rates across the different therapies is limited.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Exploring the contribution of ARMS2 and HTRA1 genetic risk factors in age-related macular degeneration.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Exploring the contribution of ARMS2 and HTRA1 genetic risk factors in age-related macular degeneration.
content.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of severe irreversible central vision loss in individuals over 65 years old. Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have shown that the region at chromosome 10q26, where the age-related maculopathy susceptibility (ARMS2/LOC387715) and HtrA serine peptidase 1 (HTRA1) genes are located, represents one of the strongest associated loci for AMD. However, the underlying biological mechanism of this genetic association has remained elusive. In this article, we extensively review the literature by us and others regarding the ARMS2/HTRA1 risk alleles and their functional significance. We also review the literature regarding the presumed function of the ARMS2 protein and the molecular processes of the HTRA1 protein in AMD pathogenesis in vitro and in vivo, including those of transgenic mice overexpressing HtrA1/HTRA1 which developed Bruch's membrane (BM) damage, choroidal neovascularization (CNV), and polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV), similar to human AMD patients. The elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the ARMS2 and HTRA1 susceptibility loci has begun to untangle the complex biological pathways underlying AMD pathophysiology, pointing to new testable paradigms for treatment.

records.title: Performances of Machine Learning in Detecting Glaucoma Using Fundus and Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography Images: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Performances of Machine Learning in Detecting Glaucoma Using Fundus and Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography Images: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the performance of machine learning (ML) in detecting glaucoma using fundus and retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) images.

Design

Meta-analysis.

Methods

PubMed and EMBASE were searched on August 11, 2021. A bivariate random-effects model was used to pool ML's diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC). Subgroup analyses were performed based on ML classifier categories and dataset types.

Results

One hundred and five studies (3.3%) were retrieved. Seventy-three (69.5%), 30 (28.6%), and 2 (1.9%) studies tested ML using fundus, OCT, and both image types, respectively. Total testing data numbers were 197,174 for fundus and 16,039 for OCT. Overall, ML showed excellent performances for both fundus (pooled sensitivity = 0.92 [95% CI, 0.91-0.93]; specificity = 0.93 [95% CI, 0.91-0.94]; and AUC = 0.97 [95% CI, 0.95-0.98]) and OCT (pooled sensitivity = 0.90 [95% CI, 0.86-0.92]; specificity = 0.91 [95% CI, 0.89-0.92]; and AUC = 0.96 [95% CI, 0.93-0.97]). ML performed similarly using all data and external data for fundus and the external test result of OCT was less robust (AUC = 0.87). When comparing different classifier categories, although support vector machine showed the highest performance (pooled sensitivity, specificity, and AUC ranges, 0.92-0.96, 0.95-0.97, and 0.96-0.99, respectively), results by neural network and others were still good (pooled sensitivity, specificity, and AUC ranges, 0.88-0.93, 0.90-0.93, 0.95-0.97, respectively). When analyzed based on dataset types, ML demonstrated consistent performances on clinical datasets (fundus AUC = 0.98 [95% CI, 0.97-0.99] and OCT AUC = 0.95 [95% 0.93-0.97]).

Conclusions

Performance of ML in detecting glaucoma compares favorably to that of experts and is promising for clinical application. Future prospective studies are needed to better evaluate its real-world utility.

records.title: Genome-wide Survival Analysis for Macular Neovascularization Development in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Revealed Shared Genetic Susceptibility with Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

content.title: Genome-wide Survival Analysis for Macular Neovascularization Development in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Revealed Shared Genetic Susceptibility with Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To identify susceptibility genes for macular neovascularization (MNV) development in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC).

Design

Genome-wide survival analysis using a longitudinal cohort study.

Participants

We included 402 and 137 patients with CSC but without MNV at their first visit from the Kyoto CSC Cohort and Kobe CSC dataset, respectively. All patients underwent detailed ophthalmic examinations, including multimodal imaging, such as fundus autofluorescence, spectral-domain OCT, and fluorescein angiography/indocyanine green angiography or OCT angiography.

Methods

We conducted a genome-wide survival analysis using the Kyoto CSC Cohort. We applied the Cox proportional hazard model to adjust for age, sex, and the first principal component. Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with P values < 1.0 × 10-5 were carried forward to the replication in the Kobe CSC dataset. Moreover, we evaluated the contribution of previously reported age-related macular degeneration (AMD) susceptibility loci. We used FUMA and ToppFun for the functional enrichment analysis.

Main outcome measures

The association between SNPs and MNV development in patients with CSC.

Results

Rs370974631 near ARMS2 displayed a genome-wide significant association in the meta-analysis of discovery and replication result (hazard ratio [HR]meta, 3.63; Pmeta = 5.76 × 10-9). Among previously reported AMD susceptibility loci, we additionally identified CFH rs800292 (HR, 0.39, P = 2.55 × 10-4), COL4A3 rs4276018 (HR, 0.26, P = 1.56 × 10-3), and B3GALTL rs9564692 (HR, 0.56, P = 8.30 × 10-3) as susceptibility loci for MNV development in CSC. The functional enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of 8 pathways (GO:0051561, GO:0036444, GO:0008282, GO:1990246, GO:0015272, GO:0030955, GO:0031420, and GO:0005242) related to ion transport.

Conclusions

ARMS2, CFH, COL4A3, and B3GALTL were identified as susceptibility genes for MNV development in CSC. These 4 genes are known as susceptibility genes for AMD, whereas COL4A3 and B3GALTL were previously reported to be polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV)-specific susceptibility genes. Our findings revealed the shared genetic susceptibility between PCV and MNV secondary to CSC.

records.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
content.abstract: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo), formerly known as peripheral benzodiazepine receptor is a highly conserved transmembrane protein primarily located in the outer mitochondrial membrane. In the central nervous system (CNS), especially in glia cells, Tspo is upregulated upon inflammation. Consequently, Tspo was used as a tool for diagnostic in vivo imaging of neuroinflammation in the brain and as a potential therapeutic target. Several synthetic Tspo ligands have been explored as immunomodulatory and neuroprotective therapy approaches. Although the function of Tspo and how its ligands exert these beneficial effects is not fully clear, it became a research topic of interest, especially in ocular diseases in the past few years. This review summarizes state-of-the-art knowledge of Tspo expression and its proposed functions in different cells of the retina including microglia, retinal pigment epithelium and Müller cells. Tspo is involved in cytokine signaling, oxidative stress and reactive oxygen species production, calcium signaling, neurosteroid synthesis, energy metabolism, and cholesterol efflux. We also highlight recent developments in preclinical models targeting Tspo and summarize the relevance of Tspo biology for ocular and retinal diseases. We conclude that glial upregulation of Tspo in different ocular pathologies and the use of Tspo ligands as promising therapeutic approaches in preclinical studies underline the importance of Tspo as a potential disease-modifying protein.

records.title: Exploring single-cell RNA sequencing as a decision-making tool in the clinical management of Fuchs' endothelial corneal dystrophy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Exploring single-cell RNA sequencing as a decision-making tool in the clinical management of Fuchs' endothelial corneal dystrophy.
content.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has enabled the identification of novel gene signatures and cell heterogeneity in numerous tissues and diseases. Here we review the use of this technology for Fuchs' Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy (FECD). FECD is the most common indication for corneal endothelial transplantation worldwide. FECD is challenging to manage because it is genetically heterogenous, can be autosomal dominant or sporadic, and progress at different rates. Single-cell RNA sequencing has enabled the discovery of several FECD subtypes, each with associated gene signatures, and cell heterogeneity. Current FECD treatments are mainly surgical, with various Rho kinase (ROCK) inhibitors used to promote endothelial cell metabolism and proliferation following surgery. A range of emerging therapies for FECD including cell therapies, gene therapies, tissue engineered scaffolds, and pharmaceuticals are in preclinical and clinical trials. Unlike conventional disease management methods based on clinical presentations and family history, targeting FECD using scRNA-seq based precision-medicine has the potential to pinpoint the disease subtypes, mechanisms, stages, severities, and help clinicians in making the best decision for surgeries and the applications of therapeutics. In this review, we first discuss the feasibility and potential of using scRNA-seq in clinical diagnostics for FECD, highlight advances from the latest clinical treatments and emerging therapies for FECD, integrate scRNA-seq results and clinical notes from our FECD patients and discuss the potential of applying alternative therapies to manage these cases clinically.

records.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
content.abstract: Patients who suffer from sight-threatening eye diseases share a desire to regain a comfortable reading ability. In light of the modern advances achieved in ophthalmic diagnosis and therapy, and because a significant lack of comparability between reading charts still exists, there is an increasing need for a worldwide standard in the form of a norm for diagnostic reading charts. Already, applied advancements such as digital print, which allow a calibration of the print sizes of reading charts in correctly progressing geometric proportions by using the actual height of a lower case "x" in millimeters (x-height), and psychophysically standardizing reading charts and their test items by applying modern statistical methods have significantly contributed to establishing a norm for reading charts. In 2020, a proposal of the British delegation was accepted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) group "Visual Optics and Optical Instruments," and a working group was established. Bearing in mind the efforts of the ISO with regard to an international norm, this review article is intended to (a) give an overview of the historical background and related normative approaches for diagnostic reading tests used in ophthalmology and optometry, (b) explain psychophysical and technical concerns, and (c) discuss the possibilities and limits of concepts that seem relevant to developing a modern standard for reading charts.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the predictive accuracy of 4 toric intraocular lens (IOL) formulas (Barrett, EVO, Hoffer QST, and Kane) integrated in the ESCRS calculator. Barrett and EVO were tested with measured (Barrett M and EVO M) and predicted (Barrett P and EVO P) posterior corneal curvature.

Setting

Multiple surgical centers in the United States.

Design

Retrospective database study.

Methods

6753 eyes implanted with nontoric IOLs were analyzed. Preoperative biometry, including posterior corneal curvature, was obtained using the IOLMaster 700. Predicted residual astigmatism was calculated through the proprietary websites of the 4 toric formulas integrated into the ESCRS IOL power calculator. Primary endpoints were the mean vector magnitude error and proportions of eyes with vector magnitude prediction errors ≤0.50 diopters (D).

Results

Kane demonstrated the lowest mean vector magnitude prediction error (0.537 D), significantly lower than EVO P (0.561 D), EVO M (0.57 D), Barrett M (0.579 D), Barrett P (0.583 D), and Hoffer QST (0.622 D) (all P < .001). This result was consistent in with-the-rule, against-the-rule, and oblique subgroups. Kane also achieved the highest proportion of eyes with prediction error ≤0.50 D ( P < .001). For all formulas, centroid values were significantly different from zero. The Kane formula showed the lowest total variances, significantly lower than all other formulas ( P < .001).

Conclusions

The Kane formula showed statistically superior predictive accuracy with the lowest errors and variances and the highest proportion of eyes within 0.50 D. However, differences among formulas were small, and their clinical relevance for toric IOL outcomes remains uncertain.

records.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To improve the accuracy of refractive prediction for pediatric secondary sulcus intraocular lens (IOL) implantation by optimizing the effective lens position (ELP) prediction within the SRK/T formula.

Setting

Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Guangzhou, China.

Design

Retrospective consecutive case-series.

Methods

The value of sulcus-ELP was identified by linear regression formula with utilizing back-calculated ELP. The obtained sulcus-ELP was subsequently incorporated into the original SRK/T formula, then creating the sulcus-SRK/T formula. The prediction accuracy of sulcus-SRK/T formula was compared with six formulas. Main outcome measures included prediction error (PE), mean error (ME), median absolute error (MedAE), and the percentage of eyes with prediction error within ±0.50 diopters (D) and ±1.00 D.

Results

This study included 86 pediatric patients (131 eyes) who underwent secondary ciliary sulcus IOL implantation. With the modified formula, the percentages of eyes achieving the prediction error (PE) within ±0.50 D and ±1.00 D were 25.6% and 53.9%, respectively, significantly higher than those of other formulas. The mean error (ME) of the modified formula was 0.46±1.39 D, and the modified formula showed lower median absolute error (MedAE) (0.95 D, P < .05) than other formulas.

Conclusions

By optimizing ELP prediction of the SRK/T formula, the prediction accuracy of pediatric secondary sulcus IOL implantation has been improved. The sulcus-SRK/T formula is a worthwhile choice and requires further external validation to confirm its effectiveness.

records.title: Incidence of secondary intraocular lens implantation in school-aged children left aphakic to age 4.5 years in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Incidence of secondary intraocular lens implantation in school-aged children left aphakic to age 4.5 years in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine the incidence of secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in a cohort of children randomized to aphakia after unilateral congenital cataract surgery.

Setting

12 clinical sites in the United States.

Design

Randomized clinical trial. Data regarding secondary IOL implantation were collected retrospectively when patients were age 10.5 years.

Methods

We calculated the cumulative incidence of secondary IOL implantation in participants in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study who were randomized to aphakia to age 4.5 years and were followed at age 10.5 years.

Results

22 (43%, 95% CI, 29%-58%) of the 51 participants left aphakic to age 4.5 years who had better than light perception vision at age 4.5 years received a secondary IOL by age 10.5. More than half (59%) of these were implanted by age 6 (median 64.5 months, interquartile range 60-80). Secondary IOLs were implanted in children with good visual acuity (≤20/40), as well as those with poor visual outcomes (≥20/200) (39% and 44%, respectively). Children who received a secondary IOL did not report less contact lens wear than those remaining aphakic (average of 94% of waking hours vs 90%, respectively). However, the proportion of children receiving a secondary IOL varied substantially by study center.

Conclusions

Many children with unilateral congenital cataract who are initially left aphakic remain aphakic throughout the elementary school years. Practice patterns and family preference seem to be important drivers of the decision to implant a secondary IOL in these children.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

records.title: Dilated Pupil Vertical-to-Horizontal Ratio as a Predictor of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Dilated Pupil Vertical-to-Horizontal Ratio as a Predictor of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate whether intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) can be predicted from pupil morphology, including vertical pupil elongation and pupillary diameter.

Setting

Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital, Shiga, Japan.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

Patients who underwent standalone phacoemulsification cataract surgery between November 2022 and April 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. In bilateral cases, only the first operated eye was included. Eyes with prior ocular surgery or conditions affecting pupil morphology were excluded. Surgical videos were reviewed to assess pupil morphology parameters, including the pupil vertical-to-horizontal ratio (PVHR) and the composite pupil-to-corneal diameter ratio (CPCDR) at the beginning of surgery, and to evaluate IFIS incidence. IFIS incidence was treated as the outcome variable. Explanatory variables comprised age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, α1-adrenergic antagonist use, and pupil morphology parameters. Associations were evaluated using logistic regression.

Results

A total of 263 patients (263 eyes) were included, of which 23 eyes (8.7%) developed IFIS. PVHR was significantly higher in eyes with vs without IFIS (median: 1.06 vs 1.03; p < 0.001), while CPCDR was significantly lower (0.56 vs 0.70; p < 0.001). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, PVHR (odds ratio: 4.06; p = 0.0005) and CPCDR (odds ratio: 0.43; p < 0.0001) were independently associated with IFIS.

Conclusions

Vertical pupil elongation and poor dilation after pharmacologic mydriasis were independently associated with IFIS. Assessment of pupil shape, in addition to pupil size, may improve preoperative identification of eyes at risk for IFIS.

records.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dysfunctional lens index (DLI), higher-order aberrations (HOA), and modulation transfer function (MTF) from ray-tracing aberrometry as objective markers of posterior capsular opacification (PCO) and treatment response.

Setting

Two tertiary ophthalmology centers, Istanbul, Turkey.

Design

Prospective interventional study with a clear-capsule pseudophakic control group.

Methods

Eyes with visually significant PCO after uncomplicated phacoemulsification with monofocal IOL implantation underwent ray-tracing aberrometry and 4 weeks after Nd:YAG capsulotomy; one eye per patient was analysed. CDVA, DLI, total and internal HOA root mean square (RMS), Zernike components, and MTF at 5-30 cycles/degree (cpd) were compared with clear-capsule control eyes with the same IOL.

Results

Thirty-one eyes of 31 patients (mean age 66.7 years; 21 female) and 28 control eyes were included. All parameters improved after capsulotomy (all P<.001): CDVA from 0.52 to 0.10 logMAR, DLI from 3.10 to 7.20, internal HOA RMS by 66.9%. Internal coma and trefoil decreased, whereas spherical aberration was unchanged (negative control). MTF improved at all six spatial frequencies. Pre-operatively, PCO eyes were degraded relative to controls (DLI 3.35 vs 7.67; P<.001); post-operatively they matched controls (7.23 vs 7.67; P=.44). DLI correlated with internal HOA (r=-0.947) and MTF (r=+0.842) but not CDVA (r=-0.051).

Conclusions

Ray-tracing aberrometry offers an objective view of PCO-induced optical degradation. Because the DLI tracks internal aberrations and MTF yet remains independent of high-contrast acuity, it captures impairment that CDVA alone overlooks, and returns to clear-capsule levels after capsulotomy. The DLI thus serves as a useful adjunctive marker for gauging PCO-related degradation and monitoring treatment response.

records.title: Ophthalmologists' Perspectives on Cataract Surgery Sedation: A National Survey Study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Ophthalmologists' Perspectives on Cataract Surgery Sedation: A National Survey Study.
content.abstract:
Descriptive abstract

In this national survey assessing US cataract surgery sedation practices, among 659 of 3,406 (19.3%) respondents, 578 (87.7%) routinely performed cataract surgery with anesthesia care. For sedation, 534 (81.0%) routinely used light-to-moderate IV sedation; 69 (10.5%) routinely used oral or no additional sedation. Forty-two (6.4%) performed cataract surgery in office-based surgery (OBS) suites. For future consideration of OBS, 76.0% (n=501), 76.0% (n=501) and 77.2% (n=509) indicated it was "moderately" or "very important" for Medicare to establish physician payment policies for OBS; to maintain access to ambulatory surgery center or hospital outpatient department privileges for complex cases; and for Medicare to continue allowing anesthesia services in the office when needed, respectively. Ophthalmologists nationwide rely heavily on anesthesia care for cataract surgery sedation. With appropriate training and favorable Medicare policies to make OBS financially viable and safe, ophthalmologists may be willing to assume additional, selected sedation roles traditionally performed by anesthesia teams.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Jacques Daviel's Summer 1750 Trip to the Meuse-Rhine Region and Newly Discovered Announcement of a Revolution in Eye Surgery.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Jacques Daviel's Summer 1750 Trip to the Meuse-Rhine Region and Newly Discovered Announcement of a Revolution in Eye Surgery.
content.abstract: Jacques Daviel (1696-1762) is credited with introducing planned primary cataract extraction. We analyzed historical books, newspapers, manuscripts, and documents discovered between 2004 and 2026, including previously unreported notices in the 1750 Gazette de Cologne. On July 7, 1750, Daviel performed an experimental crystalline lens extraction in a sheep before professors in Louvain. Although he later claimed to have performed cataract extractions in Liège, no contemporaneous documentation of those procedures survives. On September 10, 1750, he performed a witnessed sheep experiment before the Cologne medical faculty, and on September 18 performed a planned primary cataract extraction on the cleric Gilles Nouprez, whose immediate visual improvement was reported in the Gazette de Cologne. The newspaper announced Daviel's new technique on September 22, 1750, representing, to our knowledge, the earliest published documentation of planned primary cataract extraction.

records.title: OpenEvidence versus Six Leading Large Language Models in Refractive Surgery: Does Curated Medical Evidence Confer an Advantage?
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: OpenEvidence versus Six Leading Large Language Models in Refractive Surgery: Does Curated Medical Evidence Confer an Advantage?
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the accuracy of OpenEvidence relative to six leading large language models (LLMs) in answering refractive surgery multiple-choice questions, and to compare their performance with users of the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) Self-Assessment Program.

Setting

Not applicable.

Design

Randomized questionnaire-based study using 225 questions from the refractive surgery section of the AAO BCSC Program.

Methods

OpenEvidence and 6 LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and Grok) answered the same set of multiple-choice questions. Their accuracy was defined as the proportion of correct responses. Performance from 1,983 BCSC Self-Assessment Program users served as a benchmark.

Results

OpenEvidence achieved the lowest accuracy (76%) and performed significantly worse (P<0.05) than all six general-purpose LLMs. Claude achieved the highest accuracy (92%), followed by Grok (89.8%). ChatGPT-5, Copilot, and Gemini each scored an accuracy of 88%, and ChatGPT-4o achieved 86.2%. All models' lower 95% confidence interval bounds exceeded the 60% passing threshold. The average score of BCSC Self-Assessment Program users was 77%. All general-purpose LLMs scored significantly higher than BCSC Self-Assessment Program users (P<0.05), whereas OpenEvidence did not.

Conclusions

OpenEvidence demonstrated significantly lower accuracy than the six evaluated general-purpose LLMs and did not exceed the BCSC Self-Assessment program user benchmark on this standardized refractive surgery multiple-choice assessment. This task-specific difference was not fully explained by response-format noncompliance and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of globally inferior medical knowledge or performance in open-ended clinical applications.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Repeatability of an SD-OCT biometer (MS-39 AL) and agreement with a validated biometer (IOLMaster 700).
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Repeatability of an SD-OCT biometer (MS-39 AL) and agreement with a validated biometer (IOLMaster 700).
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the repeatability of biometric measurements obtained with the MS-39 AL (CSO) and to assess their agreement with those provided by the IOLMaster 700 (Carl Zeiss).

Setting

IRCCS Bietti Foundation, Rome, Italy.

Design

Prospective evaluation of diagnostic test.

Methods

Patients were classified in Group A (with cataract) and Group B (with clear lens). For repeatability analysis, three measurements were obtained with the MS-39 AL. Agreement was analyzed by comparing the first MS-39 AL measurement with the corresponding measurement by the IOLMaster 700.

Results

111 eyes were enrolled. Group A included 53 eyes (mean age: 69.4 ±7.3 years) and Group B 58 eyes (mean age 35.5 ±9.1 years). In both groups, the MS-39 AL demonstrated high repeatability for all biometric parameters, as the coefficient of variation ranged from 0.04% for axial length to 2.10% for lens thickness, except in the case of corneal astigmatism. Agreement between biometers was high for most parameters, with narrow 95% limits of agreement. Significant differences were observed for anterior chamber depth (MS-39 AL = 3.52±0.44 mm, IOLMaster 700 = 3.42±0.45 mm, p <0.0001), corneal diameter (MS-39 AL = 11.90±0.46 mm, IOLMaster 700 = 12.19±0.49 mm, p <0.0001), central corneal thickness (MS-39 AL = 531.75±31.20 µm, IOLMaster 700 = 534.80±32.79 µm, p <0.001) and lens thickness (MS-39 AL = 4.18±0.55 mm, IOLMaster 700 = 4.13±0.52 mm, p = 0.002).

Conclusions

The MS-39 AL provides highly repeatable biometric measurements and shows good agreement with the IOLMaster 700 for most parameters in both cataractous and clear-lens eyes.

records.title: Optimizing flange geometry with a 532-nm green laser for four-flanged scleral fixation: an experimental comparison with thermal cautery.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Optimizing flange geometry with a 532-nm green laser for four-flanged scleral fixation: an experimental comparison with thermal cautery.
content.abstract:
Synopsis

A 532-nm green laser was a feasible alternative to cautery, producing larger, flatter flanges at shorter heating lengths and supporting 1.0-mm laser heating for four-flanged scleral fixation.

Purpose

To compare flange geometry produced with a 532-nm green laser versus thermal cautery in four-flanged scleral fixation and to identify practical heating lengths for 5-0 and 6-0 polypropylene sutures.

Setting

Dry laboratory.

Design

Bench-top experimental study.

Methods

Flanges were created on 5-0 and 6-0 polypropylene sutures using a 532-nm green laser (200 mW, 200 ms, single-shot mode) or handheld thermal cautery. Heating length, defined as the distance from the suture tip to the forceps, ranged from 0.5 to 3.0 mm in 0.5-mm increments. Flange diameter and height were measured microscopically, and shape was summarized by the diameter-to-height (D/H) ratio.

Results

Flange diameter and height increased with heating length for both devices. The laser produced larger diameters than cautery for 6-0 polypropylene at 0.5-1.5 mm (all P < .001) and for 5-0 polypropylene at 0.5-2.5 mm (P ≤ .023). At shorter heating lengths, the laser tended to produce flatter, saucer-shaped flanges with higher D/H ratios, whereas cautery often produced taller, mushroom-shaped profiles. Using guide-needle outer diameters as practical surrogate targets (30-gauge ≈ 300 μm for 6-0; 27-gauge ≈ 400 μm for 5-0), the shortest heating length at which mean flange diameter exceeded the target was 1.0 mm with laser and 1.5 mm with cautery for both suture sizes.

Conclusions

Laser-assisted flange formation appears to be a feasible alternative to thermal cautery. In this dry-laboratory model, 1.0-mm laser heating and 1.5-mm cautery heating provided practical target flange dimensions while maintaining modest flange height.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance

US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models.

Objective

To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.

Design, setting, and participants

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.

Exposures

The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice.

Main outcomes and measures

Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

Results

Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

records.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

content.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
content.abstract:
Importance

The effect of cornea donor diabetes severity on graft success, endothelial cell density (ECD), and morphometry after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) is not known.

Objective

To determine whether graft success, corneal endothelial cell loss (ECL), and morphometric changes 1 year after DMEK are associated with cornea donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, donor's postmortem level of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and postmortem advanced glycation end products (AGEs) or advanced oxidation end products (AOPs).

Design, setting, and participants

This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter, double-masked, randomized clinical trial at 28 clinical sites (46 surgeons) and 13 eye banks in the US among individuals undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of donors. Data analysis was conducted from September 1, 2025, through April 30, 2026.

Intervention

DMEK performed with a cornea from a donor without or with diabetes, assigned using a minimization procedure (comparable to randomization) to achieve an approximate 2:1 distribution, respectively.

Main outcomes and measures

Graft success, ECL, coefficient of variation (CV) of cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells (HEX) at 1 year from eye bank and postoperative specular central endothelial images.

Results

A total of 1097 individuals (1421 study eyes; median [IQR] age, 71 [66-76] years; 631 [57.5%] female) undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK (1044 [95.2%] for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy) were included. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of 472 donors (542 study donor corneas). Among 968 eyes with a postmortem donor HbA1c level lower than 6.5%, the 1-year graft success rate was 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%), compared with 97.4% (95% CI, 93.9%-100.0%), 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%), and 95.8% (95% CI, 87.3%-100.0%) among eyes with a donor HbA1c level of 6.5% to less than 7.5% (n = 194), 7.5% to less than 9.0% (n = 86), and 9.0% or higher (n = 48), respectively (P = .72). There was no significant difference in mean ECD across donor HbA1c groups. Donor diabetes severity measured with severity score, donor HbA1c level, and AGE and AOP metrics was not associated with 1-year graft failure, ECD, CV in cell area, or HEX percentage.

Conclusions and relevance

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that ECL and morphometry 1 year after DMEK were not affected by cornea donor diabetes severity. Comparable 1-year graft success, ECL, and cell morphometrics with tissue from donors with and without diabetes, regardless of the diabetes severity biomarker values observed, support the use of corneas from donors with diabetes for endothelial keratoplasty procedures without additional preoperative testing or risk stratification based on the diabetes status of the cornea donor.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05134480.

records.title: Subbasal Nerve Plexus Alterations Following Ocular Proton Therapy in Uveal Melanoma Assessed by Corneal Confocal Microscopy.

content.title: Subbasal Nerve Plexus Alterations Following Ocular Proton Therapy in Uveal Melanoma Assessed by Corneal Confocal Microscopy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate longitudinal changes in the subbasal nerve plexus (SNP) after ocular proton therapy (OPT) in eyes with uveal melanoma and associated changes in corneal sensitivity, cell density, and patient-reported outcomes.

Design

Prospective clinical cohort study.

Subjects

Fifty-eight patients (58 eyes) with uveal melanoma were enrolled; 54 had evaluable baseline corneal confocal microscopy images, and 40 formed the longitudinal analysis cohort. Follow-up data were available for 30 patients at 3 months and 27 patients at 12 months.

Methods

Corneal confocal microscopy was used to assess SNP parameters and cell density. Corneal sensitivity was measured with a Cochet-Bonnet aesthesiometer. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the German Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) and selected domains from the German version of the NEI VFQ-25. Examinations were performed before OPT and at 3 and 12 months after OPT.

Main outcome measures

Primary outcome measures were changes in corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD), corneal nerve branch density (CNBD), and corneal nerve fiber length (CNFL). Secondary outcome measures included corneal nerve fiber tortuosity (CNFT), cell density, corneal sensitivity, OSDI, and selected NEI VFQ-25 domains.

Results

CNFD decreased from 18.2 to 11.4 (3 months) and 12.7 no./mm² (12 months) (P = .002 and .001). CNBD decreased from 23.9 to 13.5 and 15.8 no./mm² (P = .012 and .040), and CNFL from 11.0 to 6.2 and 7.3 mm/mm² (both P < .001). Nerve loss was associated with treatment-related exposure, particularly the clinical target volume. CNFT decreased at 3 months (P = .018) and approached baseline at 12 months (P = .28). Corneal sensitivity did not change significantly. OSDI increased at 12 months (P = .049). After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, the 3-month CNFT, 12-month OSDI, and 12-month cell density changes were no longer significant. Among NEI VFQ-25 domains, only peripheral vision declined (84 to 68; P = .006).

Conclusions

OPT was associated with marked reduction of SNP parameters, with only partial recovery by 12 months. Greater nerve loss was associated with larger treatment volumes and greater corneal irradiation. Cell density and corneal sensitivity remained unchanged, whereas patient-reported outcomes did not consistently reflect structural denervation.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.

content.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.
content.abstract:
Importance

Altmetric Attention Scores (AAS) measure attention to scholarly articles through social media, news coverage, or policy citations. How AAS aligns with impact factors for ophthalmic peer-reviewed medical literature remains unclear.

Objective

To assess correlations between AAS and citation metrics at the article and journal levels.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional study included all citable items published between 2022 and 2023 in a subset of ophthalmology journals indexed in the 2024 Journal Citation Reports. The top 500 articles ranked by AAS were selected as a high-attention publication subset for detailed analysis.

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was Spearman rank correlations between AAS rankings and normalized citation rankings (calculated as total citations divided by months elapsed since publication) at the individual article level and between an entire journal's AAS rankings and Journal Impact Factor (JIF) rankings.

Results

This study included 24 059 citable items in 99 journals. Among the top 500 high-attention articles, correlation between individual article-level AAS rankings and citation rankings was 0.08 (95% CI, -0.01 to 0.16; P = .08). At the journal level, correlation was 0.57 (95% CI, 0.41-0.69; P < .001). Correlations for predominantly clinical research-oriented journals compared with predominantly nonclinically or mixed research-oriented journals were 0.64 (95% CI, 0.46-0.79) vs 0.43 (95% CI, 0.09-0.69) (difference = 0.21; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.60; P = .24). Multivariable analysis showed that AAS rankings were independent of document type (review vs original article: β = -10.6; 95% CI, -47.8 to 26.6; P = .58) or publication date (per month elapsed: β = 0.7; 95% CI, -1.1 to 2.5; P = .45).

Conclusions and relevance

In this cross-sectional study of high-attention ophthalmology publications, individual article-level AAS rank was not associated with citation rank, whereas journal-level Altmetric rank was moderately associated with JIF rank and greater for clinical research-oriented journals. These findings suggest that online attention and impact factor reflect partially overlapping but distinct dimensions of research dissemination and that both metrics are independent, important variables that may contribute to judging the value of peer-reviewed medical journals.

records.title: AGE-RELATED PATTERNS OF PSEUDOMELANOMAS IN PATIENTS REFERRED FOR SUSPECTED UVEAL MELANOMA AT A TERTIARY OCULAR ONCOLOGY CENTER.

content.title: AGE-RELATED PATTERNS OF PSEUDOMELANOMAS IN PATIENTS REFERRED FOR SUSPECTED UVEAL MELANOMA AT A TERTIARY OCULAR ONCOLOGY CENTER.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the clinical spectrum and age distribution of pseudomelanomas in patients referred for suspected uveal melanoma at the largest ocular-oncology center in South Korea, where uveal melanoma incidence is the lowest worldwide.

Methods

A retrospective review was conducted of consecutive patients referred for suspected uveal melanoma between January 2020 and August 2025. Diagnoses were confirmed using multimodal imaging. Patients were stratified into five groups (0-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-80, and 81-100 years) to identify age-specific diagnostic patterns.

Results

Of 687 patients, 564 (82.1%) had pseudomelanomas and 123 (17.9%) had clinically confirmed melanoma, 81 of which had cytologic/pathologic confirmation. Common pseudomelanomas were choroidal nevus (N = 120, 21.3%), congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (N = 70, 12.4%), choroidal hemangioma (N = 53, 9.4%), choroidal metastasis (N = 39, 6.9%), optic disk melanocytoma (N = 35, 6.2%), and retinal capillary hemangioblastoma (N = 32, 5.7%). Rare entities included vortex vein varix (N = 7, 1.2%), posterior nodular scleritis (N = 6, 1.1%), choroidal lymphoma (N = 3, 0.5%), degenerative retinoschisis (N = 2, 0.4%), RPE adenoma, uveal effusion, ciliary body schwannoma, ciliary body leiomyoma (N = 1, 0.2%, respectively), etc. Uveal melanoma was absent in those aged 0 to 20 years and predominated in adults aged 41 to 80 years, along with nevus and metastasis, while congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium, retinal capillary hemangioblastoma, and choroidal osteoma were more common in patients aged 40 years or younger. Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy was predominant in patients aged 81 years or older, while primary vitreoretinal lymphoma occurred in patients 61 years or older.

Conclusion

Pseudomelanomas accounted for over 80% of suspected uveal melanoma cases in this Korean cohort, with age-specific distribution patterns. Recognizing pseudomelanomas features and these patterns may enhance diagnostic accuracy.

records.title: The lens epithelium as a major determinant in the development, maintenance, and regeneration of the crystalline lens.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The lens epithelium as a major determinant in the development, maintenance, and regeneration of the crystalline lens.
content.abstract: The crystalline lens is a transparent and refractive biconvex structure formed by lens epithelial cells (LECs) and lens fibers. Lens opacity, also known as cataracts, is the leading cause of blindness in the world. LECs are the principal cells of lens throughout human life, exhibiting different physiological properties and functions. During the embryonic stage, LECs proliferate and differentiate into lens fibers, which form the crystalline lens. Genetics and environment are vital factors that influence normal lens development. During maturation, LECs help maintain lens homeostasis through material transport, synthesis and metabolism as well as mitosis and proliferation. If disturbed, this will result in loss of lens transparency. After cataract surgery, the repair potential of LECs is activated and the structure and transparency of the regenerative tissue depends on postoperative microenvironment. This review summarizes recent research advances on the role of LECs in lens development, homeostasis, and regeneration, with a particular focus on the role of cholesterol synthesis (eg., lanosterol synthase) in lens development and homeostasis maintenance, and how the regenerative potential of LECs can be harnessed to develop surgical strategies and improve the outcomes of cataract surgery (Fig. 1). These new insights suggest that LECs are a major determinant of the physiological and pathological state of the lens.
